title: Upstream storm-overflow spills had a small negative spatial link to English river invertebrate scores in 2021-2026, but wet-year spill increases gave no detectable decrease
abstract: Question: do storm-overflow spills lower river invertebrate pollution scores in England, and do weather-driven spill changes between wet and dry years have an effect? Data: Environment Agency Event Duration Monitoring returns 2020-2025 (about 14,300 overflows each year), EA kick-sample invertebrate data (WHPT ASPT) and OS Open Rivers for along-channel links. Overflows 0-5 km downstream of a site were a negative control. The analysis plan was written before outcome models. Results: (1) Monitoring completeness increased from 74% to 92% of overflow records in 2021-2025; about one quarter of the reported 2021-2023 increase in spill hours came from this. (2) Within sites, year-to-year changes in upstream spill hours gave no detectable ASPT decrease: +0.018 per log unit (95% CI -0.004 to +0.040; 4,935 samples, 1,048 sites), which limits harm to 0.0025 ASPT per doubling of spill hours. All checks gave the same result. (3) Between sites in 2021-2026, upstream spill hours had a small negative association with ASPT relative to downstream spill hours (difference -0.034 per log unit, SE 0.010; about -0.13 ASPT at 1,000 hours per year). The same gradient was steeper with 1995-2004 ASPT, and sites near overflows in both directions recovered more since then, so this recovery is not spill-specific. (4) Sites below high-spill overflows did not lose ground after 2018 (+0.054, SE 0.029), so they do not explain the 2018-2025 autumn ASPT stall of earlier campaign work. The wet-minus-dry-year gap was -0.038 (SE 0.033), uncertain. Limitations: associations only; no water-quality, flow or effluent data; annual spill totals only; six spill years; snapping errors possible; England only.

Below: between-site models for 2021-2026, and for the same 763 sites with 1995-2004, 2010-2019 and 2021-2026 ASPT. Bars are 95% CI.

Yearly ASPT gap of high-upstream-spill sites (n=210) and high-downstream-only sites (n=190) relative to sites with no overflow within 5 km, with site x season and area x season x year fixed effects; 2010-2019 mean set to 0 (2015 is the reference year). Lower panel: spill hours of the fixed panel of 6,201 overflows.
Left: total reported spill hours and fixed-panel spill hours (overflows valid in all of 2021-2025), 2021 = 1. Right: share of overflow records with monitors that operated for 90% of the year or more.

citations.reason: Reported the open 2018-2025 autumn ASPT stall in English rivers; we tested storm overflows as a cause and found that high-spill sites did not explain it.
